title: What the brain senses
summary: Give the brain an input of your own, then try the bigger brains and see what each one adds.

steps.title: A sense of your own
steps.body:
A brain only knows what its inputs tell it. navigation-starter has 11: eight rays, two numbers for the finish and one for the path hint.

A `sensor` line adds one more input, computed by your script. Give the brain the gap to the nearest spikes, from 0 to 5 m. The range tells the app how to scale it for the brain.

The check counts the test runner's inputs. It should now be 12.
hints: A sensor line looks like sensor name "Label" in low .. high = value.
Write sensor spikeGap "Spike gap" in 0 m .. 5 m = agent.spikeDistance.

steps.title: A brain that sees more
steps.body:
navigation-standard has twelve rays, and each ray also says whether it hit spikes or a mover. It feels its own speed and the time left too: 42 inputs.

Change the brain line to `brain navigation-standard`. With your sensor that makes 43.

More inputs are not free. Each one adds weights that evolution has to tune, so a bigger brain often learns slower at first.
hints: Write brain navigation-standard on the brain line.

steps.title: No path hint
steps.body:
The path hint is an arrow along the shortest way round whatever stands in the way. It makes the early levels easy, a bit like a satnav.

navigation-advanced trades it for sixteen longer rays: 53 inputs, 54 with your sensor. Without the hint a brain has to work out the way round walls on its own, which takes far longer to learn.

Switch to `brain navigation-advanced`. The test runner now steers by the bearing to the finish alone.
hints: Only the brain line changes again.
Write brain navigation-advanced on the brain line.
